chunks: I said to him: 'A man has a child — is it permissible for him to give his wealth to his relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth. He may do with it whatever he wishes until death comes to him.'

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: Child/children — heirs who stand to inherit under Islamic inheritance rules
key_terms.قَرَابَة: Relatives, kinship connections — those related by blood outside the immediate nuclear family
key_terms.يَأْتِيَهُ الْمَوْتُ: Until death comes — the boundary beyond which inheritance rules become operative
key_terms.يَسَعُهُ: Permissibility/leeway — whether an action falls within the latitude of Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Can a person with children give their wealth to relatives instead of their heirs in Islam?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether a man with children may distribute his wealth to his relatives during his lifetime. The Imam affirmed that a person retains full ownership and disposition rights over their property as long as they are alive, and may give it to whomever they wish — relatives or otherwise — before death. This ruling affirms the principle of complete ownership rights (haqq al-tamalluk) during one's lifetime, and distinguishes pre-death gift-giving from the rules of inheritance that apply after death.
